extracted_empirical_metrics.sample_size_n: National administrative accounts (BCV / PDVSA monthly registers)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exposure_indicator: Acute political crisis & presidential overthrow attempt
extracted_empirical_metrics.outcome_indicator: Real GDP contraction & temporary oil supply dip
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_table_page: BCV Boletin Mensual / Cuentas Nacionales 2002, Cuadro 1
extracted_empirical_metrics.verbatim_quote: "En el ano 2002 la actividad economica venezolana medida a traves del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) experimento una contraccion de 8,9%... influenciada por los sucesos politicos de abril y el inicio del paro petrolero en diciembre."
extracted_empirical_metrics.causal_caveats: Macro-observational register data; political crisis acted as catalyst for subsequent December 2002 general strike.

extracted_empirical_metrics.sample_size_n: 18,000 dismissed PDVSA technical/managerial personnel (~40% of workforce)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exposure_indicator: Mass dismissal of specialized reservoir engineers and geologists; conversion of PDVSA into political patronage vehicle
extracted_empirical_metrics.outcome_indicator: Crude oil output collapse (2.90M bpd in Nov 2002 to 0.25M bpd in Jan 2003) & cumulative 2-year GDP collapse of -16.0%
extracted_empirical_metrics.unit: percent drop in daily oil extraction at trough
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_table_page: Monaldi et al. (2021), Resources Policy 72, Section 3.2, p. 5
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_line: Table 1 / Section 3.2: Personnel fired: ~18,000; output collapse from 2.9M bpd to <0.5M bpd
extracted_empirical_metrics.verbatim_quote: "Chavez dismissed around 18,000 PDVSA employees, about 40% of the total workforce, including most of the managerial and technical staff. This had a devastating effect on the company's human capital and technical capabilities, from which it never fully recovered."
extracted_empirical_metrics.causal_caveats: Permanent institutional hysteresis: reservoir depressurization and water infiltration in Lake Maracaibo fields caused irreversible damage; rig efficiency permanently lowered.

extracted_empirical_metrics.sample_size_n: Monthly national series (Jan 2013 - Jul 2017, N=55 months)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exposure_indicator: Succession of Nicolas Maduro, collapse of CADIVI FX controls, monetized fiscal deficit, hyperinflation
extracted_empirical_metrics.outcome_indicator: Pre-sanctions oil production decline & active rig count contraction
extracted_empirical_metrics.unit: barrels per day (from 2.40M bpd in 2013 to 1.91M bpd in July 2017)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_table_page: Bahar et al. (2019), Brookings Policy Brief, Figure 2, p. 4
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_line: Page 4, Paragraph 3: 'Between 2005 and 2016, daily oil output had already dropped by roughly 24%'
extracted_empirical_metrics.verbatim_quote: "Between 2005 and 2016, daily oil output had already dropped by roughly 24%... the steep downward trend in Venezuelan oil production was well established long before the August 2017 financial sanctions were imposed by the US government."
extracted_empirical_metrics.causal_caveats: Crucial distinction between pre-sanctions decline (>70% of total collapse) driven by non-payment to oil service companies (Halliburton, Schlumberger) and subsequent sanctions accelerator.

extracted_empirical_metrics.break_name: US Financial (2017 EO 13808) & Sectoral Oil Sanctions (2019 EO 13850)
extracted_empirical_metrics.sample_size_n: N = 1,800+ monthly firm-level panel observations (2008-2020) across Orinoco Basin JVs
extracted_empirical_metrics.exposure_indicator: Prohibition of US debt financing (EO 13808) & designation of PDVSA on SDN list with import/diluent ban (EO 13850)
extracted_empirical_metrics.outcome_indicator: Firm-level monthly crude oil production in Orinoco Basin joint ventures
extracted_empirical_metrics.unit: barrels per day output reduction among credit-accessible SFV firms
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_table_page: Rodriguez (2022), Latin American Economic Review 31:6, Table 2 & Abstract, p. 1
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_line: Abstract, lines 4-9; Table 2 baseline DiD regression results
extracted_empirical_metrics.verbatim_quote: "We use the differential access to credit of oil firms in Venezuela's Orinoco Basin to identify the economic effects of financial and oil sanctions on firm output. Using a panel of monthly firm-level oil production from 2008-2020, we provide difference-in-differences estimates showing that financial and oil sanctions led to large oil production losses among firms that had access to international credit prior to sanctions. The estimated effects explain around half of the output drop experienced in those firms since the adoption of sanctions, for a total loss of around USD 6.2bn a year at current oil prices."
extracted_empirical_metrics.causal_caveats: Identifies treatment effect specific to joint ventures with pre-existing Special Financing Vehicles (SFVs); macro-level oil drop reflects combination of pre-sanctions maintenance starvation, electrical grid blackouts (March 2019), and sanctions embargo on diluents.

extracted_empirical_metrics.break_name: Post-2022 OFAC General Licenses (GL 41 Chevron / GL 44 Temporary Relief)
extracted_empirical_metrics.sample_size_n: Monthly national production (Nov 2022 - Dec 2024, N=26 months)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exposure_indicator: OFAC GL 41 authorization of Chevron crude exports to US; GL 44 6-month broad temporary relief
extracted_empirical_metrics.outcome_indicator: Crude oil extraction rebound from sanctions trough
extracted_empirical_metrics.unit: barrels per day increase (from ~680 kb/d in Nov 2022 to ~850 kb/d in 2024)
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_table_page: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR) Dec 2024, Table 5-8: Secondary Sources
extracted_empirical_metrics.exact_line: Venezuela secondary sources: Nov 2022 (683 kb/d) vs Oct 2024 (850 kb/d)
extracted_empirical_metrics.verbatim_quote: "Secondary sources reported that Venezuela's crude oil production averaged 850 tb/d in late 2024, up from 683 tb/d in late 2022, primarily driven by joint venture activities under OFAC General License 41."
extracted_empirical_metrics.causal_caveats: Recovery strictly contingent on US extraterritorial licensing regime; capacity capped by lack of pipeline infrastructure, diluent availability, and legal uncertainty.
